summary: Iteration 2 — validated (a) Emergent Google-auth gating on /hub and /settings and (b) multi-tier LLM routing (NVIDIA → Emergent → YABBAI) end-to-end. 12/12 backend tests pass (3 skipped by design because the env already has NVIDIA + YABBAI configured; the graceful-degradation path is still covered by a snapshot/clear/restore test). Frontend gate + settings UI works: unauthenticated /hub and /settings redirect to /login; with a seeded session_token cookie the hub renders the shell (signed-in email, live strip, 5 green service cards, civilisation map, ⚙ Routing & Connections link, Sign out link), and /settings renders 3 tier cards with up/down/toggle controls, an active-routing flow strip, nvidia-key / yabbai-url / yabbai-key inputs and a Save button. Reorder + Save persists and secrets never echo back raw. Logout invalidates the session. Regression check on /api/network/status and /api/revenue/api/status still green.

ui_bugs.issue: The Save button (data-testid=settings-save) is enabled and clickable BEFORE the async load()/render() completes. If a user clicks it during the ~1-2s load window, the JS `order` array is still [] and the PUT wipes route_order to [] server-side. Reproduced in this run — required manual restore. Fix: keep the button disabled until render() finishes, or refuse to submit when order.length === 0.

issues: Kill-switch chip 🛑 still an inline-onclick element with no data-testid (carry-over note from iter_1).
The `.svc .sport` port labels (e.g., :7870, :8001) are now misleading in the unified single-port deployment — all services live under /api/<name> on :8001. Cosmetic only.

action_items: settings/index.html: disable the Save button (or the reorder arrows) until load()/render() has populated `order`, else a click during load wipes route_order in Mongo.
Optional: on the backend, treat empty `route_order` in PUT /api/settings as a no-op (or reject) — defensive server-side guard against the same bug from any client.
Cosmetic: update the port labels in hub/index.html (`{port:7870}` etc.) to reflect the unified :8001 deployment.
critical_code_review_comments: network_db.save_settings drops blank/'********' secrets (good) but does NOT similarly guard against empty lists like route_order=[] — a client bug can silently wipe routing config. Add a check.

ai_router._order() falls back to ['emergent'] if the active list is empty, so chat still works — but /api/ai/providers.active_order becomes [] which is what confused the settings UI flow strip briefly. Consider defaulting active_order to DEFAULTS['route_order'] when the stored list is empty.

settings/index.html:106 `S = await fetch(...).then(r=>r.json())` has no error handling — if /api/settings ever 5xx's, the page will look 'loaded' (auth check passed) but tier cards never render and the still-enabled Save button becomes a footgun.
auth_router expires_at parsing handles both str and datetime — good; but no test coverage for the string branch. Not blocking.

rca of the issue: Empty route_order bug — RCA: settings/index.html initializes `let order = []` and only populates it after `S = await fetch('/api/settings')` resolves inside load(). The Save button is rendered as static HTML with data-testid=settings-save and is clickable from t=0. Clicking Save before load() completes serializes order=[] and PUTs it, which network_db.save_settings persists as-is because empty list is not a secret-field blank. Reproduction: (1) seed a session, (2) navigate to /settings, (3) within ~1s click [data-testid='settings-save'] → GET /api/settings shows route_order=[]. Mitigation: disable the Save button until render() runs (set a boolean `loaded=false` at top, flip in render()); AND in backend save_settings, ignore payload keys where key=='route_order' and the value is an empty list.
